Antenatal Care

Antenatal care — booking visit, schedule, examination, danger signs, anaemia and immunisation in pregnancy.

🎯 After this chapter you can

  • Describe the antenatal visit schedule
  • Take a booking history and examination
  • List antenatal danger signs
  • Give antenatal nutrition and advice

In simple words

Antenatal care protects the mother and baby before birth. The aim is to prevent, detect and treat problems early and to prepare the mother for a safe birth.

Schedule of visits

Period Number of visits
First 6 months (to 32 weeks) One visit each month
Seventh and eighth months (32-36 weeks) One visit every 2 weeks
Ninth month (36-40 weeks) Weekly

At least 4 antenatal visits; the WHO recommends 8 contacts.

Booking visit — history

  • Name, age, height, weight, blood group
  • Obstetric history: gravida, parity, previous births, abortions, stillbirths
  • Menstrual history — LMP, cycle regularity
  • Medical history — hypertension, diabetes, heart disease, previous surgery
  • Family and social history
  • Immunisation status

Antenatal examination

  • Blood pressure — 120/80 or above is a danger sign
  • Weight — sudden gain indicates oedema and pre-eclampsia
  • Pallor — anaemia
  • Fundal height — correlates with weeks of gestation
  • Fetal heart rate — 110-160 per minute
  • Fetal position, presentation — after 36 weeks
  • Oedema — feet, face and hands
  • Urine — albumin and sugar

Investigations

  • Blood: Hb, blood group and Rh, VDRL, HIV, HBsAg, sugar tolerance, haemoglobin electrophoresis
  • Urine: albumin and sugar and microscopy
  • Ultrasonography: fetal growth, anomalies, position, placenta

Antenatal danger signs

  • Bleeding per vagina
  • Severe or persistent headache
  • Blurred vision
  • Sudden swelling of face and hands
  • Severe upper abdominal pain
  • Reduced or absent fetal movement
  • Fever with chills
  • Gush of fluid (leaking membranes)

🔴 Reduce fetal movement is an emergency

A mother who reports reduced fetal movements must be seen the same day. Absent fetal movement, bleeding, high blood pressure with headache and blurred vision all need urgent referral.

🔴 Most important for exams

  1. ANC schedule: monthly to 32 weeks, fortnightly to 36 weeks, then weekly.
  2. At least 4 visits recommended; WHO advises 8 contacts.
  3. Examination: BP, weight, fundal height, fetal heart rate, pallor, oedema.
  4. Reduced fetal movement is an obstetric emergency.
  5. First visit includes Hb, blood group, HIV, VDRL, urine and ultrasound.

⭐ Important for exams

  1. Iron, folic acid and calcium tablets are given routinely.
  2. Tetanus toxoid is given twice during pregnancy.
  3. Naegele’s rule estimates EDD as LMP plus 9 months plus 7 days.
  4. Anaemia below 11 g/dL is treated and referred.
  5. Birth planning includes transport, blood and the place of birth.

📌 Memory trick

Danger signs = B-B-V-F-R: Bleeding, Blurred vision, Vomiting severe, Few fetal movements, Raised BP.

60-second revision

  • ANC: four to eight visits with increasing frequency.
  • Book early, examine BP, weight, pallor, fundal height and fetal heart.
  • Investigations: Hb, group, HIV, VDRL, urine, ultrasound.
  • Danger signs: bleeding, headache, blurred vision, swelling, reduced fetal movement.
  • Iron, folic acid, calcium, TT vaccine, birth planning.

Test yourself

The minimum number of antenatal visits recommended in India is:

Answer: B. A minimum of four planned visits is recommended under the Indian programme; WHO advises eight contacts.

Normal fetal heart rate is:

Answer: B. A normal fetal heart rate is 110 to 160 per minute.

Sudden swelling of face and hands in pregnancy may indicate:

Answer: B. Facial and hand oedema with headache or raised blood pressure suggests pre-eclampsia and needs referral.

Tetanus toxoid is given during pregnancy:

Answer: B. Two doses of tetanus toxoid protect mother and newborn from neonatal tetanus.

Reduced fetal movement means the mother should:

Answer: B. Reduced fetal movement may indicate fetal hypoxia and must be assessed immediately.
